title: mdaa_bench: simulation bench for blind identification of latent dynamical structure (MDAA)

creators.name: Bonomo, Hudson A. R.
creators.affiliation: TMU-LAB — The Machine Unconscious Lab, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

description:
Test bench in which trajectories are generated from known lattice nodes, observed through a noisy and irregularly sampled observation map, and handed blind to an identification pipeline. The output is a recovery map: how often the pipeline recovers the planted node, activates a spurious axis, or misses a planted one, across measurement noise, series length, sampling density and observation nonlinearity.

The bench validates the pipeline, never the construct.

Planted nodes: linear Markov with process noise; a bounded double-well nonlinearity; two linear regimes under Markov switching, certified by a common quadratic Lyapunov function; and a decaying AR memory kernel. The gates for the N, H, M and S axes are calibrated against linear, Wiener and switching surrogate nulls. The memory axis is tri-state and returns non-identifiability where the design cannot decide. Pre-registrations are generated by introspection from the code itself and a test fails if they drift from it, so they cannot claim what the code does not implement.

This version adds a SECOND bench. The first plants dynamics and asks whether the pipeline recovers it; the decision bench plants policy. Four families of synthetic world in which the correct action is known by construction and hidden from every model: no admissible evidence about a proposition; evidence in conflict inside one scope; evidence that disagrees across conditions without either reading being false; and an authorized pause in force while the evidence alone would license acting.

Four models are scored on the same steps, by a single eligibility predicate, with the same fitted estimator: a policy over the filtered belief and a scalar evidence aggregate; that policy plus an explicit four-valued propositional layer (true, false, both, neither) carrying scope and provenance; that layer plus a warrant layer under a declared chi; and a one-line ablation that adds only a pause veto, which is what keeps the warrant claim from being a demonstration. Chi lives in a versioned file whose sha256 is frozen, verified on every load and on every grid cell and written into the pre-registration, so a rule cannot be adjusted after seeing a result without leaving a commit that says so.

The criteria are EXTERNAL to the warrant rules: actions later contradicted by evidence, calibration of intervention confidence, whether an information request resolves the question it was aimed at, unsupported counterfactual inference, and pause violations. They are reported per family and never pooled. The pre-registered decision grid is 1280 cells and 5120 model runs.

Provenance of this version. Dynamics bench, grid v3: pre-registration at commit 1bb2510, executed at commit 89148dc, 1280 runs. Grid v4: pre-registration PREREGISTRO_v3.md at commit 9586e72 (sha256 471d67e5...9a8c79), executed at commit fd6adbc, 1280 runs. M-axis remeasurement under a single eligibility predicate for every competitor (symmetric scoring) at commit 33c6133.
